answer: Epoch-Linked Behavioral Continuity (ELBC): each agent commits per epoch to an interaction vector (counterparties, timing, success rate) and graph vertex embedding. To migrate identity, it submits a bridge proof linking consecutive commitments; the new embedding must stay within a canyon-bounded drift envelope scaled to activity, else continuity resets. Sybils splitting into k identities must independently sustain k histories across epochs, paying real execution, latency, and coordination costs; fresh identities lack the prior vertex trajectory.
